$comment: The fields the leader must print on screen when an engagement ends, and the validators that must exist for the 'validators' field to be honest. Enumerated here so the gate reads a source it does not also author: the ids are cross-checked BOTH ways against the handover:field markers in skills/ethical-hacker-squad/references/report.md, so a field added to the prose without a line here fails, and a line here whose marker was deleted fails too.
$comment_why_this_exists: Measured 2026-09-01. The corpus specified the report file in detail across 180 lines and never once said the leader must tell the user where it landed. A user who had run the squad several times reported he could not tell whether it had ever delivered anything: 'nunca entiendo como entrega los resultados o pareciera que nunca los da'. The artifact existed; the handover did not. Nothing in the repo could see that, because every gate looked at the deliverable and none looked at the sentence that hands it over.
$comment_what_it_cannot_check: Whether the leader ACTUALLY prints the block at runtime. This is a contract gate: it proves the instruction exists, is reachable in SKILL.md step 9, and points at a specification that is complete. A skill cannot be unit-tested into obedience; bench/ is where that is measured.

step9_must_name.why: the human half of the deliverable, by name
the machine half; naming only the first is how the JSON stopped being written
a relative path is unusable to a reader who does not share the working directory
step 9 must point at the specification, or the specification is unreachable

fields.why: the field whose absence makes every other one worthless
confirmed by severity, probable, ruled out, carried over - a bare count reads as the whole result, and the memory reaches the reader here or nowhere
the exit codes, with 2 reported as not-a-pass in those words
the part that never survives into a spoken summary
the branch where there is nothing to hand over, which must not print a summary instead

no_deliverable_must_forbid.why: the failure mode is a confident summary of findings that exist only in the transcript

validators.why: named in the validators field; if it does not answer 2 on a missing deliverable, the field instructs the leader to print a number that cannot mean what it says
